bull_bear.body: Final dividend INR 7.5/share recommended. Reinvestment priority on backward integration (HyCO plant with Praxair) and downstream polymerization to capture value chain spread. Debt drawdown linked to equity infusion milestones (25% equity for 40% debt tranche).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Technical stability of new Concentrated Nitric Acid (CNA) plant (ran at 45% util in Q4 due to issues). 2) Geopolitical escalation affecting Strait of Hormuz logistics. 3) Chinese regulatory enforcement timing/intensity. 4) Sulfur cost inflation.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and opportunistic; emphasized 'agility' in supply chain management and 'structural' advantages of integration. Transparent on CNA technical glitches but firm on FY27 improvement trajectory.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly linked Q4 margin beat to a contrarian 'buy every dip' feedstock strategy initiated in Jan/Feb based on US aircraft carrier movements, creating an inventory buffer that paid off during Q4 price spikes. Also, the Polycarbonate project uses a 'Build-Own-Operate' model with Praxair for HyCO to reduce upfront capex and execution risk.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend is shown only as 'Dividend as % of Face Value' across FY20-FY26 with the values 225%, 225%, 350%, 375%, 375%, 375%, 375% plus a 50% figure, against a three-part legend (Special / Final / Interim). The chart's label-to-value binding is lost in extraction, so the per-year and per-type split is NOT asserted here.
- Under 'Consistently Rewarded Shareholders', market cap is given as INR 87.7 bn ($0.9 bn) on 31 July '20 versus INR 226.7 bn ($2.4 bn) on 31 July '26, at a stated conversion rate of INR 95.43 per dollar (Source: FEDAI).
- Reinvestment commitments disclosed: 'around 2,900 Cr' for the Polycarbonate project and 'over INR 100 Crore' for the Savli R&D Centre.
- The CMD frames 'disciplined capital allocation' - alongside integrated operations, secure feedstock access and strong process capabilities - as what makes companies 'preferred long-term partners'.
- The deck presents no balance sheet, net debt, gearing or cash flow data, so leverage and funding of the capex programme are not addressed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Advanced Intermediates: Rev INR 708 Cr (+8% YoY), EBIT INR 34 Cr (vs INR 15 Cr Q3); driven by optimized mix. Phenolics: Rev INR 1,429 Cr, EBIT INR 287 Cr (20% margin); benefited from stable ops and improved spreads despite feedstock volatility.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High freight costs and supply chain disruption from Middle East conflict blocking Strait of Hormuz; working capital blockage in imports. | Deepak Nitrite Ltd | beneficiary | High | Domestic customers shifting to Deepak for JIT supply to avoid import volatility; company captured margin upside via low-cost inventory while competitors faced spot price spikes. |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as 'one of the leading producers of chemical intermediates in India' and the 'Largest Producer of Phenol, Acetone, IPA & Sodium Nitrite in India', recognised globally as a 'Responsible Manufacturer' and as a 'Supplier of Choice' by marquee customers.
- Rich legacy of over 5 decades; products exported to 50+ countries across 6 continents; 1,500+ customers and 6,100+ total workforce.
- Macro tailwinds map cites China+1 diversification ('a trusted, globally competitive alternative supply chain for intermediates and specialities') and 'Targeting the massive structural supply gap in India for engineering polymers and advanced materials'.
- Deck claims 'Deepak Group to become one of the few global players to achieve full integration across ammonia-nitration-amines spectrum'.
- Credit ratings stated as ICRA AA Stable (long-term) and ICRA A1+ (short-term).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group vs listed entity] Several strategy claims and the entire CMD message are framed around 'Deepak Group', and the Polycarbonate build is described as 'DCTL's Polycarbonate project' - not explicitly attributed to the listed entity Deepak Nitrite Limited on a standalone basis.
- [Structure] Manufacturing sites are attributed to multiple entities - DNL, DCTL, DAML, DPL, DCLT (as printed, for Sankarda) and DOIL (Oman) - with no shareholding or consolidation map provided.
- [Digitalisation] 'Digital initiatives include SAP S/4HANA migration, AI/ML-driven smart manufacturing, optimize power and predictive analytics through a Digital Innovation Lab'.
- [Regulatory] Growth drivers cite alignment with 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' for import substitution, benefit from PCPIR infrastructure, and 'Strong Government backing'.
- [Disruption landscape] Named headwinds: geopolitical tensions and shifting trade dynamics, aggressive global (especially China-led) pricing, logistics disruptions and freight volatility, feedstock constraints, energy cost volatility and 'Potential demand softness'.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margins (18%) boosted by proactive low-cost feedstock procurement (benzene, xylene, toluene) ahead of geopolitical spikes. Cost headwinds noted in sulfur downstream (sulfuric acid/Oleum), but net impact neutralized by nitration chemistry tailwinds from Chinese regulatory constraints.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Q1FY27 expected to be better than Q4FY26 on both standalone and consolidated basis. Margins: FY27 to see stronger margin profile driven by new high-margin products and normalization. Order Inflow: Stable domestic demand; export recovery expected as logistics normalize. Capex: INR 11,000 Cr total program; Polycarbonate commissioning targeted June 2028; MIBK/MIBC commissioning Q1/Q2 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A (Make-to-stock/order model); however, management highlights 'wallet share' retention and stable domestic supply commitments replacing import dependency for customers.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) MIBK/MIBC commissioning in Q1/Q2 FY27. 2) 6-7 new agrochemical/custom molecules reaching commercial scale by Q3 FY27. 3) Fluorinated molecule plant (INR 220 Cr) validation complete, regular production Q3 FY27. 4) India's first fully integrated Polycarbonate facility (June 2028).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Deepak Nitrite leveraged strategic feedstock inventory builds ahead of Middle East tensions to drive a 74% QoQ EBITDA surge in Q4FY26, offsetting technical teething issues in new nitric acid capacity. The thesis pivots on FY27 margin expansion from new agro-chemical products and the long-term value unlock of the integrated polycarbonate complex commissioned by 2028.

open.item: Shri Maulik Mehta has been re-appointed and elevated to Deputy Managing Director with effect from May 9, 2026 for five years, and Shri Meghav Mehta has been elevated and appointed as Deputy Managing Director with effect from May 9, 2026 for five years, both subject to shareholder approval.
The multipurpose agrochemical intermediates and MIBC/MIBK projects are scheduled for commissioning in Q2 of FY 2026-27.

A dividend of Rs 7.50 per equity share, being 375% of the face value of Rs 2.00 each, has been recommended by the Board for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, and is to be paid within 30 days of the AGM, i.e. on or before September 4, 2026.
open.promised: 7.50 per equity share (375% of face value) INR per share

open.item: Shri Anant Pande is proposed to be appointed as Whole-time Director designated Executive Director & Chief Manufacturing Officer for three years with effect from August 5, 2026 up to August 4, 2029, in place of Shri Ajay C. Mehta who retires by rotation and has not offered himself for re-appointment.
Renewable power momentum is expected to continue through enhanced renewable power substitution at existing plants and expansion to additional facilities in FY 2026-27.
Execution of a fully integrated polycarbonate facility, a first for India, is on track.

Deepak Chem Tech Limited has entered into a strategic long-term agreement to establish a dedicated on-site HyCO plant at its Dahej facility under a Build-Own-Operate model, reducing upfront investment for the polycarbonate resin project.
New products in the area of Material Sciences are being considered based on the core competencies of Deepak.
The Company will continue advancing downstream projects MIBK/MIBC and the polycarbonate initiative to move toward high-value, application-driven segments.
The Company will continue to increase the share of renewable energy in its operations and reduce its carbon footprint.
The Company intends to further consolidate its position across the ammonia-nitration-amines value chain to gain control over critical inputs and capture higher value across the chain.

Across all nine NGRBC principles the Company states it has not set any specific goals with timelines, and will assess its strategic positions and develop specific goals, targets and commitments with timelines in due course — a deferred ESG target-setting commitment to track.

The Company has appealed before the State Appellate Authority a demand for ineligible Input Tax Credit for FY 2019-20, stating it believes the ITC was availed after following the due process of law and complying with GST-law conditions.

Long-term group captive agreements for renewable power for Gujarat and Maharashtra facilities are expected, upon commissioning, to replace approximately 70% of conventional power consumption with renewable energy.

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR materiality assessment as a Risk with negative financial implications if unaddressed. Management states that given the energy and water-intensive nature of chemical production, failure to reduce the environmental footprint can have significant repercussions on standing within the industry and on relationships with customers, investors and society. Physical as well as transition climate risks are described as directly associated with disruptions to the Company's operations and those of its value chain partners. Mitigation is via sustainable manufacturing practices, reducing utility consumption, extracting value from waste, adopting clean technologies and keeping effluents, emissions and waste within Pollution Control Board limits.
risks.risk: Climate change and emissions exposure inherent to energy- and water-intensive chemical production

risks.note: Flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Given the inherent nature of operations, employees face a range of operational and safety hazards; process safety gaps and OHS incidents could harm employees, jeopardise production targets and adversely affect assets, environment and business reputation. Mitigated through stringent site-level safety measures, regular safety audits, provision of appropriate PPE, and safety awareness campaigns and training.
risks.risk: Occupational health, safety and process-safety incidents

risks.note: Flagged as a Risk. Amid escalating macro-economic volatility in the chemical industry, meeting regulatory compliance requirements and effectively managing risk is described as paramount; failure would have severe financial implications, since governance is increasingly the parameter for evaluation by external stakeholders. Mitigation rests on the Board's composition and independent thinking, a robust code of conduct, a comprehensive risk management framework and focused Board Committees (Audit, Risk Management, Nomination and Remuneration, CSR, Sustainability), supported by a legal compliance management tool that tracks compliance across factories and offices with automatic regulatory updates.
risks.risk: Corporate governance and regulatory compliance failure

risks.note: Explicitly identified as a Risk in the BRSR materiality table — having a sustainable supply chain is described as critical for the Company's operations and business continuity given the size of the Company's supplier base (the disclosure is truncated in the routed source).

Classified as both Risk and Opportunity: the stated risk is reputational damage and negative impact on market share. DNL has established a protocol to assess the ESG impacts of products during their development stages, has calculated the carbon footprint for most of its products and plans to conduct Life Cycle Assessments for a few existing products.
risks.risk: Product stewardship — reputational damage and market-share loss from ESG impacts of products

risks.note: The Directors' Report states the Company faced subdued demand in select agrochemicals products due to sluggish global and domestic consumption, accompanied by pressure on realisation due to sustained dumping by Chinese suppliers — a structural pricing overhang on a core end-market.
risks.risk: Chinese dumping and subdued agrochemical demand compressing realisations

risks.note: Management states it remained alert to external pressures including raw material cost swings and tightening environmental norms, responding with proactive sourcing diversification, operational optimisation and enhanced customer focus. The FY26 fourth quarter saw disruption in established supply chains, logistics and freight challenges with the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz, leading to scarcity in availability and volatility in prices of crude oil and related feedstocks.
risks.risk: Raw material cost swings, feedstock/crude volatility and tightening environmental norms

risks.note: The tariff measures announced by the U.S. administration reshaped trade patterns across chemicals; while direct impact on the Company's operations remained limited due to its focus on import substitution, a diversified portfolio and balanced market presence, these measures influenced global pricing, customer procurement strategies and export competitiveness in certain product segments, and changed competitive intensity, demand patterns and investment decisions.
risks.risk: Global trade-policy shifts and tariff measures affecting export competitiveness
